paragraphs: CCTV Installation is arranged by iComply Property Services from the workshop at 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport, Cheshire SK2 5DE. This guide is for landlords, letting agents and commercial occupiers. The work is price on application after the building, the existing equipment and the access are known. Nothing on this page is a fixed fee, a day rate or a pound figure.

The scope for CCTV Installation is written as six practical items: camera positions, lens and night view, recorder retention, cable routes, remote-viewing accounts and signage and privacy masks. Each item is confirmed against the site. Camera positions is agreed first, because the rest of the job hangs on it. Lens and night view is checked on site rather than copied from a previous quote. Recorder retention is included when the survey shows it is required, and left out when it is not. iComply does not pad CCTV Installation with equipment you did not ask for and do not need.

Cable routes is part of CCTV Installation when the building needs it. Remote-viewing accounts is recorded in the handover so the next person is not guessing. Signage and privacy masks is the item that is most often missed when a job is sold as a box of parts. This guide keeps that item in the survey for CCTV. If one of these six items does not apply, the quote says so in writing instead of leaving a blank.

People asking for CCTV Installation are usually landlords, letting agents and commercial occupiers. A landlord, an agent or a facilities lead can instruct the job. The person who meets the engineer needs the keys, the codes and, where a recorder or controller already exists, the login. Occupied buildings are booked around the people who live or work there. Void and empty units are booked around access from the agent. CCTV Installation is not sold as a remote product with no one on site when the work needs a door, a panel or a camera to be seen.

The survey for CCTV Installation can start from photos and a postcode, and it finishes on site when the hardware has to be handled. We note the existing CCTV equipment, what still works, and what has failed. A system fitted by someone else can still be repaired or extended when the parts and the passwords allow it. If the existing kit cannot do lens and night view, we say so and quote a replacement of that part rather than promising the old unit will cope. Cabling, power and mounting are looked at before anyone talks about a new head-end.

We do not leave a shared installer login as the only way to see the system. If a follow-on visit is needed, it is a new quote, not a surprise return.

paragraphs: Access Control Maintenance is arranged by iComply Property Services from the workshop at 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport, Cheshire SK2 5DE. Access control maintenance checks readers, power supplies, door loops and the fire-release path before a resident is stuck. This guide is for landlords, letting agents and commercial occupiers. The work is price on application after the building, the existing equipment and the access are known. Nothing on this page is a fixed fee, a day rate or a pound figure.

The scope for Access Control Maintenance is written as six practical items: reader test, supply test, door loop, fire release, token sample and a service note. Each item is confirmed against the site. Reader test is agreed first, because the rest of the job hangs on it. Supply test is checked on site rather than copied from a previous quote. Door loop is included when the survey shows it is required, and left out when it is not. iComply does not pad Access Control Maintenance with equipment you did not ask for and do not need.

Fire release is part of Access Control Maintenance when the building needs it. Token sample is recorded in the handover so the next person is not guessing. A service note is the item that is most often missed when a job is sold as a box of parts. This guide keeps that item in the survey for access control. If one of these six items does not apply, the quote says so in writing instead of leaving a blank.

People asking for Access Control Maintenance are usually landlords, letting agents and commercial occupiers. A landlord, an agent or a facilities lead can instruct the job. The person who meets the engineer needs the keys, the codes and, where a recorder or controller already exists, the login. Occupied buildings are booked around the people who live or work there. Void and empty units are booked around access from the agent. Access Control Maintenance is not sold as a remote product with no one on site when the work needs a door, a panel or a camera to be seen.

The survey for Access Control Maintenance can start from photos and a postcode, and it finishes on site when the hardware has to be handled. We note the existing access control equipment, what still works, and what has failed. A system fitted by someone else can still be repaired or extended when the parts and the passwords allow it. If the existing kit cannot do supply test, we say so and quote a replacement of that part rather than promising the old unit will cope. Cabling, power and mounting are looked at before anyone talks about a new head-end.

On the day, the written scope for Access Control Maintenance follows the list you accepted. The engineer deals with reader test and supply test, then proves door loop. Results are written in ordinary language: what was found, what was changed, and what was left as it was. Passwords stay with the instructing client. We do not leave a shared installer login as the only way to see the system. If a follow-on visit is needed, it is a new quote, not a surprise return.

Handover for Access Control Maintenance includes the practical points landlords, letting agents and commercial occupiers ask for later: how to set or view the system, who has a token or an account, and where the records are. Fire release and token sample are shown to the person on site, not only written on a delivery note. Signage, privacy and fire release are called out when they apply to this access control job. The note names the building. It is not a generic certificate with the town filled in afterwards.

Limits are part of the page, not a footnote. Door hardware is chosen for the door in front of us, including fire release where the door must open on alarm. iComply does not claim a scheme badge for access control. Grade claims, scheme badges and police-response wording are not invented to decorate Access Control Maintenance. If a standard is relevant, it is named as the practice we design against, not as a badge iComply prints for itself. Gas work is not part of this security job. Where a site also needs a gas visit, that visit is carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers and is quoted separately.

Price on application means the quote follows the survey. Camera count, door count, cable runs, night lighting, access equipment and whether the building is occupied all change the figure for Access Control Maintenance. Travel from 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport, Cheshire SK2 5DE is inside that quote for towns on the Manchester and Burnley dual ring. There is no catalogue fee on this page and no 'from' price. A multi-site estate is quoted per site or as a programme, and the email says which.

Coverage for Access Control Maintenance is the dual ring: towns within 50 miles of Manchester together with towns within 50 miles of Burnley, including the Greater Manchester core. That set is 269 towns. It is not the UK top-5000 list used for nationwide fire, barrier and AOV pages, and it is not shrunk to the 60-town core. Each town has its own page so the local paragraph can name the county, the published population where we have one, and the miles from Manchester and Burnley. The parent page stays this hub. Town pages link back here and to the access control service page.

Related work sits beside Access Control Maintenance but is not silently included. CCTV, access control, door entry, intercoms and intruder alarms are separate services with their own hubs. A car-park barrier is not an ANPR camera and is not a maglock. If your site needs more than one of those, the survey splits them so the quote is readable. This guide links to the parent service and to a related security hub rather than to a dead end.

The reply is a price-on-application quote for reader test, supply test, door loop, fire release, token sample and a service note. Work starts after you accept that quote. The town page adds the local paragraph for the building you named.

After Access Control Maintenance, the useful test is simple. For cameras, can the right person export a clip from the day of the visit. For doors, does the token open the door and does fire release let it go. For alarms, can the keyholder set and unset, and does the sounder run when it should. For intercoms and door entry, can the handset call the door and release it. If that test fails, the job is not finished, even if the equipment is on the wall. That standard is how a service note is judged on this maintenance brief for access control.
